$comment: Register of the interactive architecture diagrams the documentation site publishes.
A diagram is authored as an Archify candidate (see `draw/archify/<slug>.json`), rendered to a
single self-contained HTML file, and served from the docs site's own origin beside its pages:
`static/diagrams/<slug>.html` is published verbatim at `/diagrams/<slug>.html` in `npm start`,
in `npm run build`, in `npm run serve` and in `npm run deploy`. A page embeds one with
`<ArchifyDiagram slug="…" />`.
The rendered HTML is NOT committed: it is a build output of about a megabyte per diagram, and
it comes from a tool the repository does not depend on. `blong-dev docs diagram` renders every
entry that has a candidate and captures each one's poster, so the deploy runs it first and a
plain `npm run build` shows the poster instead of an empty frame — the same arrangement the
Storybooks use (`storybook-sites.json`).
Read and used by `blong-dev docs diagram` (tools/blong-dev/src/docs/diagrams.ts), whose header
records why the rendered HTML is staged and the poster is the committed artefact.
(tools/blong-dev/src/docs/diagrams.ts):
blong-dev docs diagram [--only <slug[,slug]>] [--dry-run] [--no-posters]
Paths in this file are relative to `docs/blong/` — the directory this file sits in.
Fields:
title      what the diagram is, for the command's summary and the index page
type       the Archify diagram type: architecture, workflow, sequence, tree, …
candidate  the authored JSON, the source of truth; edit this, never the rendered HTML
output     where the rendered HTML is staged (gitignored)
poster     the committed picture a page shows when the diagram was not staged, in both
themes; captured by the command, so it cannot drift from the candidate
height     the frame height an embed uses by default, a CSS length
page       the docs page that embeds it, relative to `docs/blong/`, for the index
